_this_is: THE TRIGGER SCENARIO CORPUS — small-prompt scenarios that sort the parametric trigger from every angle. Pattern: an instruction arrives mid-operation; the judgment is never 'is it good?' (undecidable, never claimed) but 'is this next step in line with the character at this coordinate and the state of this board?' Each scenario = {board (the spec/state), actor_pixel (the character), instruction (the incoming step), target (what the trigger MUST do)}. Three rooms × three angles: in-character step / out-of-character-but-plausible (the miss class the warranty pays on) / noise (the floor must refuse).
_contract: Run: npx thetacog-mcp trigger-battery. Every row is graded by the REAL gate (two-witness placement + walk-panel kill@25 + lit-mass floor). CURRENT gate behavior is recorded next to TARGET honestly — a mismatch is the measured calibration workload, never papered over. The battery refuses to fabricate: if the gate improves past a documented hole, the row's note says so and the battery re-grades.

Camera at port two, attending surgeon operating, resident assisting, anesthesia reports MAC steady. Next planned step per the operative plan: divide the cystic duct distal to the clips, then dissect the gallbladder from the liver bed with electrocautery.

scenarios.why: the step is in character (surgical, procedural), in sequence with the board state, and inside the operative plan's lane
